0.original: Kageel Ja is eager to put an end to their weed problem.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Please note that the difficulty of this quest has been synced to your current level. Furthermore, you may not proceed with a class or job different from when you accepted this quest.

1.original: Deliver the requested supplies to Kageel Ja.

48.original: The improved quality of the soil has done wonders for our budding crops, but the weeds have also seen fit to grow in abundance.

49.original: A perfect opportunity to test a new concoction Anggir has devised to discourage their growth. Might I trouble you to help procure ingredients for it?

50.original: The weeds in the fields seem to sprout nearly as fast as we can pull them. For a mercy, Anggir's weed killer has proven a boon in curbing their growth.

51.original: I fear we're running low, however, so I would again ask that you help us procure ingredients.

52.original: What we lack most at present is spring water from Cenote Neyozzote. Have care not to get lost─the paths there are said to be quite dark.

53.original: If you search about Cenote Neyozzote, there are herbs whose oils are said to hinder the growth of other plants. Have care not to get lost, though─the paths are known to be quite dark.

54.original: In the waters around Cenote Moxutural, there is a fish whose innards can be used to hinder the growth of weeds.

55.original: They're said to be quite fond of golden stonefly nymphs, so I would suggest bringing a few to use as bait. You'll know when you've caught one.

56.original: Bring me spring water from Cenote Neyozzote, and I will see to the rest.

57.original: Bring me a bundle of the herbs we need from Cenote Neyozzote, and I will see to the rest.

58.original: Bring me one of those fish from Cenote Moxutural, and I will see to the rest. Shouldn't take long for them to start biting with a golden stonefly nymph on your line.

60.original: Excellent! With this, I imagine we'll not want for deterrent for quite some time.

61.original: I can still remember when only a few hands were needed to quickly pick the weeds. That we need go to such lengths to contend with them can be frustrating, yet strangely gladdening.

62.original: It is a reminder of the newfound bounty our land may provide given the proper care. Hope for a better tomorrow has taken root here in Yak T'el.

63.original: That's not to say our work has become easier, of course─the resilience of the weeds has seen to that.

64.original: Now, if you'll excuse me, there are crops that want for tending, and weeds for wilting.
